uncertain.note: sic. Checked letter by letter at 10x: P V R L I M E N T (the second sort is a pointed V, not A; the fifth is a plain serifed I with symmetrical top and bottom serifs, not the three-barred E of 'DE'). Spaced capitals, closed up per §3; the head ends with a comma, and 'TOLOSE' has no H.

uncertain.text: ſent (duquel eſt incertain, ſ'l eſt vif ou mort) auant que
uncertain.note: the word is printed ſ + apostrophe + l, with no i: at 9x only a comma-shaped mark sits between the long s and the l, at the same height as the apostrophe of 'l'hiſtoire' four lines below, and there is no stem or dot. Compare 'ſ'il' on the line 'ans, ſ'il n'y a nouuelles certaines du mari, ne ſoit', where the i prints clearly. Read as 'ſ'l' (the i failed to print or was omitted); it could be intended as 'ſ'il'.

uncertain.text: Ille meos primus, qui me ſibi iunxit amores,
uncertain.note: the two Latin verse lines (Aeneid IV) are set in a larger italic and indented. Transcribed as a paragraph block of two lines, not as two headings: they are a quotation of running verse, not a display title (§6). 'iunxit' is set as 'iun xit' and 'Abſtulit:ille' / 'ſecum,ſeruétque' are set tight; normalized per §1.

uncertain.text: ttouuées aſſez certaines (le mari eſtant mort à la guerre)
uncertain.note: sic: the first two sorts are both t (each has a crossbar and a foot curving right at 6x), so 'ttouuées' for 'trouuées'.

uncertain.text: uoyoit certificatoire de ſa mort, ou luy-meſme en per
uncertain.note: the mark between 'luy' and 'meſme' prints as a small round dot at mid x-height, well above the baseline where this fount sets its periods; read as a worn hyphen ('luy-meſme'), but it could be read as a period.

uncertain.text: eſtre par tout repandu de ſa mort {u}. Car bien que la
uncertain.note: the marker is a two-stroke italic glyph identical (overlaid at 14x) to the {u} marker on p004 and to the margin key u of this page; it is not the single hooked stroke of the p004 {t} marker or of this page's margin key t. Transcribed as printed, {u}. By the printer's alphabet the marker here should be t (the margin note with key t is printed beside line 'ttouuées aſſez certaines (le mari eſtant mort à la guerre)', three lines above, exactly the offset the other notes keep), so this may be a wrong sort. Reconciler should decide between {u} as printed and {t} as intended.

uncertain.text: res & cõmunes, ne ſoit concluante, ne receuë {u}. Toutes.
uncertain.note: second {u} marker on the page: same glyph as the one on 'de ſa mort', so the page prints the key u twice and no {t} and no {x} anywhere in the body. Also, 'Toutes.' ends the line with a period although the word runs on as 'fois' on the next line (sic); the mark sits at the baseline, unlike the mid-height dot of 'luy-meſme'.

the key of this note is printed as an italic b (ascender loop at the top left, bowl on the baseline at the right; no descender), while the body marker it answers is a clear italic q with a descender, in 'ſoit contentée de faire attendre la femme, cinq ans {q}:'. Both are transcribed as printed, so key b has no marker and marker {q} has no note; the b is almost certainly a wrong sort for q.
the note with key t has no {t} marker anywhere in the body of this page; see the entry on 'eſtre par tout repandu de ſa mort {u}.', where the marker prints as u.

the note with key x has no {x} marker anywhere in the body; lines 'firoit, de monſtrer…' to 'ue, par bruit & fame ſuffiroit {y}.' were checked at 3x and carry only the two u markers and the final y. Also the raised tick after the first c is read as an apostrophe ('c'veniens'); it sits at x-height, higher than the baseline periods of 'veniens.' and 'j.' on the same line, but the citation is presumably 'c. veniens' (X. de teſtibus).
the initial is the swash italic capital of this fount, whose V is drawn with a rounded left stroke and can be read as U; transcribed V for 'Vergile'.

a column of small marks runs down the outer edge of the margin block beside the notes keyed o, p and b (after 'c. vij.', 'vxores', 'diuor', 'ſed e', 'nup'), all at the same x and all sitting below the baseline of their lines; taken as show-through or set-off, not as printed periods, so no final period is transcribed on those lines. The notes lower down (keys r to y) show no such column and their real periods are transcribed.

a small ring is printed immediately after 'Iuſtin' at x-height, touching the n. It may be a superscript o abbreviating 'Iuſtinien' (the parallel note keyed r spells 'Iuſti-/nien' out), or it may belong to the column of edge marks; not transcribed.

the line is justified and the last word fragment is set as 'v e' with a gap as wide as the word space; closed up to 've' (continuing as 'lit.' on the next line, i.e. 'velit') per the spacing rules of §1/§3. A reader could equally transcribe 'v e'.

uncertain.text: Paſſez leſquels huit ans, ſe ſeroit à elle
uncertain.note: the two lines after TEXTE. are set in a noticeably larger roman; transcribed as a paragraph because they are the running quoted text of the arrest, not a display title. The last line ends 'Ar' (A plus a lightly inked r, no hyphen), the word continuing on the next page.
the foot carries the signature 'A iiij' (three minims and a j) and no catchword; the foot of the page is otherwise blank, with no foot citation block.
